title.en: Хочу: a thing or an action?

summary.en: Look after the desire word to see which construction follows.

body.en:
From season 1, episodes 2 and 3.

Forms of **хотеть** (*to want*) work in two clean patterns at the inn: followed directly by a noun for a thing someone wants, or followed by an infinitive for an action someone wants to do.

At breakfast, Kira offers a choice of nouns: **вы хотите кофе или чёрный чай?** (*do you want coffee or black tea?*). When a speaker wants to *do* something, the second verb stays in its dictionary infinitive while only **хотеть** changes for the person: **хочу увидеть хозяина чемодана** (*I want to see the owner of the suitcase*), **я почти хочу спать здесь** (*I almost want to sleep here*), and **я хочу честно извиниться** (*I want to apologise honestly*).

Notice how **хотеть** shifts its stem consonant across persons: **хочу**, **хочешь**, **хочет** in the singular, then **хотим**, **хотите**, **хотят** in the plural.

On replay, catch the form of **хотеть** first and immediately listen to the next word—a noun names the desired item, while an infinitive names the desired action.
